title: adaptive-notification-suppression-and-incident-context-enrichment-2026
author: Maya Chen
body:
SUMMARY:
This document defines the Adaptive Notification Suppression (ANS) pattern and the Incident Context Enrichment (ICE) pipeline used by Redwood platform teams to reduce alert noise while preserving actionable signal for oncall engineers. ANS is an automated decision layer applied to incoming alerts before notifications are sent; ICE augments the selected alerts with enriched context (recent traces, top-k related changes, recent deploys, cost impact) to accelerate triage.

Scope:
- Applies to all production SLO-backed alerts emitted by platform services, including: runtime-proxy, request-router, kv-prefix-cache, batching-orchestrator, and tenant-sentinel.
- Not intended for security or compliance alerts (those follow security-and-compliance/incident-response-security policies).

Goals:
- Reduce redundant notifications from cascading or repeated symptoms by >= 60% for alert classes identified in the first 30 days of deployment.
- Maintain median actionable-alert latency <= 120s for P0/P1 events after suppression decision.
- Attach contextual payload to notifications containing a top-5 diagnostic summary.

OWNER & ESCALATION:
- Product/Feature owner: Maya Chen (Platform Observability)
- Implementation & maintenance: Observability Squad (eng-platform)
- Oncall flow owner: Eng SRE (primary escalation)

SERVICE DEFINITION AND PLACEMENT:
- ANS runs as a stateless policy service behind the platform-alert-gateway. The service consumes normalized alert events from the telemetry-bus (Kafka topic: alerts.normalized.v2) and publishes decisions to alerts.dispatch.v2.
- ICE is implemented as a serverless enrichment worker (lambda-style) that subscribes to alerts.dispatch.v2 and calls data sources: traces-api, prometheus-query-proxy, deploys-store, cost-aggregator.

SUPPRESSION RULES (policy examples):
1) Aggregation windowing: if identical alert fingerprint occurs > 3x from a single cluster within 2 minutes, synthesize a single notification and mark subsequent occurrences as suppressed.
2) Symptom de-duplication: match upstream symptoms via correlation keys (root_cause_id) and suppress downstream symptom alerts for 10 minutes unless severity escalates.
3) Grace thresholds: for noisy infra (e.g., preemptible-GPU pools) apply a higher suppression window (15m) for severity=warning.
4) Dynamic SLO-aware throttling: when a service is degraded but SLO breach risk is low (<5% error budget spend in 1h), reduce alert volume by prioritizing unique-fingerprint events only.

CONFIGURATION TABLE (selected fields):
| field | type | example | notes |
| AlertWindowSizeMinutes | int | 2 | aggregation sliding window |
| MaxUniqueNotificationsPerClusterPerMinute | int | 1 | enforces fanout cap |
| SymptomCorrelationTTL | int(seconds) | 600 | how long downstream symptoms remain suppressed |
| EnrichmentTimeoutMs | int | 1500 | ICE should attach context within this time or send partial payload |

IMPLEMENTATION STEPS (high-level rollout checklist):
1) Canary: deploy ANS to region-us-west-2 behind a canary route with 1% of traffic.
2) Telemetry: enable verbose logging for canary (trace-id, fingerprint, decision-reason).
3) Metrics: onboard suppression metrics to the platform SLI dashboard (suppression.rate, suppressed_alerts_per_minute, latency.decision_ms).
4) ICE integration: wire enrichment sources and verify top-5 diagnostic fields appear in notification payloads.
5) Ramp: increase coverage to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7/14/21-day windows, evaluating suppression precision and oncall feedback after each step.
6) Rollback safety: maintain a quick toggle in k8s config map (ans.enabled) and a feature-flag gate (ff:ans_opt_out_<team>) to disable for specific tenants.

NOTIFICATION FORMATS & CHANNELS:
- PagerDuty (critical): include ICE payload + last 3 logs (log-ids) + recent spans summary.
- Slack alert channel (ops-#): trimmed ICE summary, link to full incident page.
- Email (ticketing): full ICE payload and remediation checklist.

OPERATIONAL METRICS & DASHBOARDS:
- Primary dashboards (eng-platform/dashboards):
  - ANS Overview: suppression.rate, decision.latency_p50/p95, suppressed_alert_reasons (top-k)
  - ICE Success: enrichment_success_rate, enrichment_latency_ms, datasource_error_rate
  - Oncall Impact: mean_time_to_ack_for_actionable_alerts, false_negative_rate_estimate (sampled)

ALERTS FOR THE ANS/ICE SERVICES:
- ans-decision-latency.p95 > 2s for 5 minutes -> PagerDuty to Observability squad (P1)
- enrichment-source-failure-rate > 5% for 10 minutes -> Slack to observability-infra and auto-fallback to minimal payload (no ICE)
- suppression-queue-lag > 30s -> Oncall (P1), possible backpressure to telemetry-bus

INCIDENT TRIAGE PLAYBOOK (step-by-step):
1) Validate: check ANS Overview dashboard and recent decision logs to ensure the event reached ANS.
2) Determine scope: use ICE payload links to fetch top-5 related traces and deploy history.
3) Escalate if needed: if symptom correlation identifies a cross-service root cause, page service owner and follow cross-service SRE runbook.
4) If suppression appears overly aggressive: toggle ans.enabled=false for the service via feature flag and re-evaluate.
5) Postmortem: tag the incident with suppression.decision_id and include a sample of suppressed events for regression analysis.

EXAMPLE CLI & JSON SNIPPETS:
- Toggle feature flag (example):
  curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_API' https://featureflags.internal/v1/toggle -d '{"flag":"ans_opt_out_payment","enabled":false}'

- Example normalized alert event (ingested):
  {
    {"service":"request-router",}
    {"fingerprint":"req-router-503-xyz",}
    {"severity":"critical",}
    {"timestamp":"2026-03-02T12:02:10Z",}
    {"metadata": { "cluster":"us-west-2a", "trace_id":"abcd1234" }}
  }

- Example decision emitted (partial):
  {
    {"decision":"notify",}
    {"reason":"unique-fingerprint-escalation",}
    {"enrichment_ref":"ice/evt/2026-03-02/abcd1234",}
    {"suppress_count":0}
  }

SAMPLING & QUALITY-GUARDRails:
- We will sample one suppressed event in every 30 occurrences and attach it to the suppression-audit stream for nightly review.
- Quarterly evaluation: Observability squad will run a precision/recall evaluation on suppression rules against labeled triage data sets and iterate thresholds.

RETROSPECTIVE CHECKPOINTS (post-rollout):
- 7 days: initial noise delta analysis and oncall survey.
- 30 days: suppression precision report and false negative audit.
- 90 days: policy lineage audit and TTL adjustments.

KNOWN RISKS & MITIGATIONS:
- Risk: Over-suppression causing missed P0s. Mitigation: strict whitelist for P0 sources and heartbeat checks that bypass suppression.
- Risk: ICE introduces latency to notifications. Mitigation: enrichment timeout and partial payload fallbacks; decision path retains immediate notify when latency budget exceeded.

RELATED ARTIFACTS & LINKS:
- Implementation repo: git.internal/redwood/ans-service (README contains deployment manifests)
- Dashboard: /dashboards/ans-overview (internal)
- SLI onboarding playbook: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/platform-observability-sli-onboarding-playbook-2026.json

APPENDIX: QUICK CONFIG EXAMPLE (k8s ConfigMap snippet)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: ans-config
data:
  ALERT_WINDOW_MINUTES: "2"
  MAX_NOTIFS_PER_CLUSTER_PER_MIN: "1"
  SYMPTOM_TTL_SEC: "600"
  ENRICHMENT_TIMEOUT_MS: "1500"

If you are implementing or operating ANS/ICE, contact the Observability Slack channel (#observability) and reference this page. For feature exceptions or tenant opt-outs, work with the Platform Product manager to complete an opt-out request ticket.
